title: After-hours kernel jotter — microtriage and quick wins
content:
Context:
Quick end-of-day scratchpad for follow-ups and tiny experiments to try overnight. Not a formal runbook — personal brain dump with commands / hypotheses / what to check in morning.

Summary of what I saw today:
- P99 spike between 18:12–18:34 UTC on acct-489 (small bursts from e2e-test harness). Spikes correlate with: cold-starts to new model shard + small batches (batch_size=1) + KV cache miss storms.
- One kernel OOM that recovered after process restart (no core dump collected). Likely fragmentation + aggressive prefetch.
- Troublesome regression after PR 2119 (kernel scheduling tweak) — increased latency variance for short sequences.

Immediate triage items (priority order):
1) Reproduce: cold-start kv miss storm
   - script: tools/repro/cold_kv_storm.py --model rdx-13b --clients 40 --reqs 600 --seq 64
   - metrics to capture: per-request kv_miss_rate, tail_latency_ms, cpu%(main), cuda_mem_used, nvlink_errs
   - hypothesis: cache warm-up + simultaneous KV population causes lock contention on KV map. Try replacing one global lock with sharded locks (simple) to see effect.

2) Micro-rollback: PR 2119 scheduling tweak
   - quick A/B: deploy commit before/after to a single canary node pool (canary-4) with golden traffic generator
   - expected: variance drop if scheduling change is root cause

3) OOM root cause triage (kernel crash at 20:03)
   - check node logs: /var/log/redwood/runtime/node-153/oom.log (grab dmesg around timestamp)
   - correlate with trace IDs from tracer: trace b3-6b2a... (see trace map in observability)
   - adhoc hypothesis: quantized op path + aggressive prefetch queued > memory highwater -> allocator refusal -> crash. Lower prefetch_window and re-test.

Tiny experiments to run overnight (cheap, non-invasive):
- Prefetch window sweep: [0, 2, 4, 8] for the suspected model family, 10k requests each, measure p50/p95/p99.
- Batch shaping: implement quick flag to prefer micro-batching for seq_len <= 64 (limit batching window to 6ms), compare latency vs throughput.
- KV cache sharding proof-of-concept: copy kv map impl to kv_map_sharded.h (4 shards) and run unit stress. If passes, add to staging build.

Commands / snippets to drop in runner (notes):
- curl -X POST $CANARY_GEN/api/run -d '{"clients":40,"reqs":600,"model":"rdx-13b"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- sudo journalctl -u rwd-runtime -S "2024-10-15 18:00:00" -U "2024-10-15 18:40:00" | grep -i oom
- gdb --batch --ex "thread apply all bt" -p <pid> > /tmp/oom-backtrace.txt (if pid collected)

Observations to check first in morning:
- Are there any nvlink/pcie ECC warnings? (hardware issues sometimes look like kernel oddities)
- Did the canary A/B revert show improvement? If yes, we ship quick rollback branch.
- If KV sharding reduces lock time but increases memory, that's acceptable for short term; follow-up: optimize shard memory layout.

Open hypotheses and questions:
- Could the scheduler tweak simply expose an existing race in the prefetched-kv destructor path? Need instrumented build with sanitizer for rdma/free-ordering.
- Is the increase in variance specific to small-seq traffic patterns (LLM chat style) or also seen in long seq (batch scoring)?
- Are we seeing cross-tenant interference from noisy neighbor autoscaler actions? Check pod scaling events near spike.

Quick wins to prioritize (if time):
- Add KV map shard_count togglable via runtime flag: --kv-shards=4
- Add a short-circuit for prefetch when gpu_mem_free < 0.15 * gpu_mem_total
- Improve OOM diagnostic: dump allocator stats to /tmp/alloc-stats-<ts>.json on sig-oom hook

Notes to self (personal):
- Remember to add unit test for kv map iteration under concurrent insert+erase (race I eyeballed at 14:03).
- Ping Mina about possible memtier usage in reproducer (she suggested a lighter client harness last sprint).
- If rollback is needed, coordinate with infra (pager duty for node pool change) and schedule a 30-min window in morning slack #deploys.

Log snippets (copied from console at 18:22):
- "[warn] kv_cache miss storm: 438 misses in 5s, hits: 12"
- "[err] kernel: cudaMalloc returned CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at op conv_fwd, size=2.4GB"

Meeting follow-ups:
- Add short agenda item to morning SRE sync: "canary A/B results + KV sharding flag" (5min)
- 1:1 w/ Ravi tomorrow 10:30AM to review PR 2127 notes and plan rollback if required.

Timeboxed todo list for tomorrow (my queue):
- 30m: add simple kv_shards flag + unit test scaffold
- 45m: run prefetch window sweep on staging cluster (non-canary)
- 20m: draft rollback notes and pin exact commit to deploy if A/B fails

End-of-day micro-reflection:
- Felt we were chasing noise mid-afternoon; need to tighten reproducibility criteria before wide remediation.
- Keep the overnight runs narrow and instrumented — we don't want broad invasive changes while traffic active.

Random TODO capture (brain dump):
- Investigate whether cudaMemPool behavior differs on the new driver image (driver 525.x -> 530.x). Is that rolled to canary infra?
- Add a timestamped marker in traces when prefetch kicks in (makes it easier to correlate KV miss -> prefetch).

-- Daniela
